frozen: 2026-10-31, before any run of the changes below. Known before freezing: plan_strength_20261031.json and its results (output/polity_strength_20261031/strength.json; reports/POLITY_STRENGTH_20261031.md): the Rome-Parthia fit was uninformative because the Parthian seats were placed inside the Cliopatria polygon being scored (balanced accuracy 0.993 at every gamma); Han-Xiongnu and Tang-Turgesh results by gamma with density camps inside the steppe polygons.
change: Each polity's network comes from sources independent of the polygon it is scored against. Rome AD 150: Hanson's towns and the Itiner-e roads of AD 150 (unchanged). Parthia AD 150: its royal and vassal capitals from the literature (Isidore of Charax, Parthian Stations; Strabo; Pliny), listed below with approximate coordinates, snapped to land at 9 km. Xiongnu c. AD 2 (blind test): the excavated Xiongnu elite centres of the 1st c. BC - 1st c. AD (Brosseder & Miller 2011, Xiongnu Archaeology), listed below. Han AD 2: the county seats (unchanged). The rule and the gammas are as plan_strength_20261031.json: a land cell goes to A when d_A / k_A < d_B / k_B, k_p = (F_p / sqrt(F_A F_B))^gamma, F_p the modelled people within 2 year-round days of p's sources; gamma in {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5}.
fit: gamma maximising the balanced accuracy of Rome AD 150 against Parthia AD 150 (Cliopatria polygons; ties to the smaller gamma), window lat0 35, lon0 42, 3600 x 2400 km, 9 km cells (as the first plan)
test_blind: Han AD 2 against the Xiongnu with the excavated centres as the Xiongnu sources, in the E3 steppe window (lat0 41, lon0 106, 4200 x 2800 km, 9 km): balanced accuracy at the fitted gamma against gamma 0
tests_seen: the first plan's two steppe contests (density camps) at the fitted gamma, reported; Tang-Turgesh's centres (Suyab, Talas) lie outside the steppe window, so it has no city version
adopt_if: the fitted gamma > 0, the blind test gains >= 0.005 at that gamma, and neither seen contest loses more than 0.01. Otherwise nothing changes on the maps.
